title: Coal or oil in 2024?
hook: Oil passed coal as the biggest source of world fossil CO2 in 1968. Which led in 2024?

knows: that the world moved from coal to oil
that a share can fall while the total rises (history:industrial-co2-share)
doesNotKnow: that oil passed coal in 1968 but coal took the lead back in 2005
that coal's tonnes of CO2 in 2024 were about three times 1968's

misconception: Coal is a fuel of the past: oil replaced it.
objective: The learner can say that in the world's fossil CO2 record coal made 96% in 1900, oil was ahead only from 1968 to 2004, coal led again from 2005 and made 41% against oil's 32% in 2024, and that coal's emissions in 2024 were about 3 times those of 1968.

claims.text: World fossil CO2 by source, every year 1750-2024, in million tonnes: coal, oil, gas, and 'Other' (the total minus those three) (stage: stacked shares and tonnes).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, owid-co2-data.csv, row World, columns coal_co2, oil_co2, gas_co2, co2, 1750-2024, rounded to 0.1 Mt in Demo.tsx. 'Other' is co2 - coal_co2 - oil_co2 - gas_co2 (the file's cement, flaring and other-industry columns are not drawn separately). World row only: no country named (care line). Brief claim 1.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Re-derived in my own node script from the pinned file (history-data.mjs pins all hold; sha256 re-checked) and compared with the copied array in Demo.tsx (identical). RAW coal/oil/gas/co2 in Demo.tsx = World row rounded to 0.1 Mt, 1750-2024 (275 values each, 0 mismatches). Codebook (opened) defines coal_co2, oil_co2, gas_co2, co2 in Mt.

claims.text: In 1900 coal made 96% of the world's fossil CO2 (stage label 'Coal 96%' at 1900; readout 'Coal 1900 96%'; reveal).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, World 1900 coal_co2 / co2 = 95.9%. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 17 (reveal value c1900 = 96).

claims.text: Oil's CO2 was above coal's in 1968-2004 (37 years), and coal has been ahead every year from 2005 (hook and question: 'Oil passed/overtook coal … in 1968'; stage bracket 'oil ahead, 1968-2004'; reveal 'coal took the lead back in 2005').
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, World, years where oil_co2 > coal_co2: 1968 to 2004 (1968: oil 5,528 Mt, coal 5,320 Mt). history-cycle2-check.mjs section 17 ('oil ahead', 'coal back'). Demo.tsx AHEAD computes the same years from the rounded series.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): oil_co2 > coal_co2 in exactly 1968-2004 (37 years, contiguous); coal ahead every year 2005-2024. 1968: oil 5,528.2, coal 5,319.7.

claims.text: In 2024 coal made 41% of the world's fossil CO2 (15,805 Mt) and oil 32% (12,471 Mt) of 38,599 Mt; shares at the presets: 1968 coal 41%, oil 43%; 2005 coal 39%, oil 37% (stage labels; readout 'Coal, oil 2024 41%, 32%'; reveal).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, World 2024 coal_co2 15,805.3, oil_co2 12,470.6, gas_co2 8,009.8, co2 38,598.6. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 17 ('2024'). 1968 and 2005 shares from the same columns (node, builder, 2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 2024: coal 15,805.3 (40.9%), oil 12,470.6 (32.3%), gas 8,009.8, total 38,598.6; 1968 41.2/42.8; 2005 38.8/37.3. The denominator includes cement, flaring and other industry. That matches the Global Carbon Budget's 'fossil CO2' term (OWID metadata: 'fossil fuels and industry'), so 'fossil CO2' is right.

claims.text: Coal's emissions in 2024 were 3 times those of 1968, so a fuel can lose first place and still burn more (readout 'Coal since 1968 ×3 tonnes'; tonnes view; reveal).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, World coal_co2 2024 15,805 Mt / 1968 5,320 Mt = 2.97, shown as 3. history-cycle2-check.mjs section 17 ('tonnes').

claims.text: Where it stops: these are estimates rebuilt from records of fuel use (reveal). HELD: the one held source sentence. Fallback if not checkable: 'Where it stops: these are estimates, and the file is revised every year'.
claims.source: OWID co2-data README and the Global Carbon Project methods (README reachable at raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/co2-data; not opened for this sentence). Brief claim 3, held.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Held sentence checked against an opened source: OWID metadata for these indicators (raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/etl/master/etl/steps/data/garden/gcp/2025-11-13/global_carbon_budget.meta.yml, line 165): 'Fossil CO2 emissions are estimated using national statistics on energy use - such as coal, oil, and gas consumption - and industrial production'. recall.question: Buses carried 90% of a city's trips in 1950 and 40% today, while all trips grew six times. Did bus trips fall?
recall.why: 40% of six times the trips is 2.4 units against 0.9 before: bus trips grew about 2.7 times. Losing share is not losing volume, as coal's tonnes tripled while its share fell.
